definition: the close-relationship skills a good first conversation buys none of

settled:
They are validation, acknowledgment, reassurance and emotional intimacy.

Each one is sustained, stateful and affective: hold what the other person is feeling as it shifts, and keep meeting it turn after turn.

None of them is what makes a first conversation go well, and being good at that conversation buys none of them.

They are different skills rather than a harder version of the first-contact ones, so each needs its own build.
